angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 385,418 km at 121.01 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.2637 +/- 0.0225 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 121.01 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.554 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Incha et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-416 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract): 385,418 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.548 +/- 0.012 solar masses from Incha et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-416 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3746 +/- 72 K from Incha et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-416 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Incha et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-416 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-416.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.690, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
